newsitem.title: UK: AIDS fisherman 'slept with up to 1,000 tourists'.
newsitem.headline: AIDS fisherman 'slept with up to 1,000 tourists'.

text.p: A Greek Cypriot fisherman sentenced to 15 months in jail for negligently giving the AIDS virus to his British lover has boasted that he slept with up to 1,000 woman tourists in Cyprus, according to a London newspaper.
"I have slept with 800 to 1,000 women," The News of the World tabloid quoted Pavlos Georgiou as saying before he was sentenced in Larnaca, Cyprus, on Thursday.

"I have done everything and your British girls are the easiest. Local girls want us to promise that we will marry them before they invite us to their bed," he was quoted as saying by The News of the World.
"But that is nonsense. Why wait when we can find some less careful foreign girl for a good night? We know they are easy and then two weeks later they go home and we can forget about it."
Georgiou was convicted for infecting his former British girlfriend Janette Pink with the HIV virus that causes deadly AIDS.
Under a decades-old law enacted to curtail cholera on the eastern Mediterranean island, he faced a maximum sentence of two years in jail or a fine of 1,500 Cyprus pounds ($2,770).

Georgiou, who has tested positive for HIV, has not developed full-blown Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome and shows no sign of suffering any disease. He is on a triple drug regimen designed to delay the onset of AIDS.

The News of the World quoted Georgiou as boasting just before he was sentenced: "Many of the British girls I have slept with came to Cyprus just for the sex. Sex was so available that I never had to pay a woman for it."
